detail.longDescription: In Python 3.13 I can do this: >>> x: int >>> Which passes. But this raises NameError: >>> x Traceback (most recent call last): File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module> NameError: name 'x' is not defined In that case what is x: int doing? Is it just ignored by the Python interpreter? I understand that it is annotating the variable, but just don't understand what exactly the interpreter executes.
